RFC2865-1.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 after D-8. The recorded weak verdict named the missing clause: an Accept authorizing an unavailable service through an attribute other than Service-Type, for example Framed-User over Framed-Protocol SLIP on the L2TP LNS. That clause is now asserted: TestRFC2865AcceptForAFramingTheLNSLacksIsRejected sends Framed-User with Framed-Protocol 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (every RFC 2865 Section 5.7 framing but PPP) and 255, and fails if the session comes up; TestRFC2865AcceptForPPPFramingIsHonored sends Framed-User over PPP and fails if it is refused. Service-Type is Framed-User in both, so only the framing varies. Producer: doRADIUS refuses unless radius.AcceptedFramedProtocol(resp, FramedProtocolPPP); an absent Framed-Protocol is accepted (TestRFC2865SupportedServiceTypeIsHonored carries none and is honored, so no regression). The author observed the negative red at Framed-Protocol 2 before the fix; the gate records are panic breaks on AcceptedFramedProtocol (positive) and doRADIUS (negative). The Service-Type units on the admin and L2TP paths are unchanged and still cover the Service-Type route. Service and framing are the two attributes RFC 2865 uses to authorize a service (Section 1.1 names ARAP, a framing, as its example), so both routes are now enforced.

RFC2865-2.5-1.note: TestRFC2865RetransmitRepeatsIdentifierAuthenticatorAndSourcePort drives a real retransmit through Client.Exchange (first datagram unanswered), asserts the attribute octets unchanged first, then byte-compares the Identifier, all 16 Request Authenticator octets and the source addr:port of every retransmit against the first. A client that re-encoded with a new ID or authenticator, or opened a new socket, goes red. The {single-polarity: positive} annotation holds: a same-ID MUST has no inbound input to refuse. TestClientRetransmit remains a floor assertion.

RFC2865-3-1.note: Positive: Decode accepts 20- and 4096-octet packets (16 attributes kept) and EncodeTo writes exactly 4096 with Length 4096. Negative: Decode refuses 19 octets, refuses a 4097-octet packet whose Length field says 4097 and whose attributes are all valid (so only the maximum can refuse it), and EncodeTo refuses attributes making 4097 octets. Both bounds now discriminated at both edges.

RFC2865-3-2.note: Forbidden: a Request Authenticator that is not 16 random octets, or one drawn from a predictable source. TestRFC2865RequestAuthenticatorRandom substitutes crypto/rand.Reader and asserts the authenticator equals the substituted octets byte for byte (a counter or constant goes red), and asserts two successive values differ; the width is the [AuthenticatorLen]byte type. Single-polarity marker on the row covers the missing negative.

RFC2865-3-3.note: Forbidden: a Response Authenticator computed over anything but Code+ID+Length+RequestAuth+Attributes+Secret. TestRFC2865ResponseAuthenticatorMatchesTheFormula compares ResponseAuthenticator with an independent MD5 over exactly those fields (red on a wrong formula, with a non-degenerate attribute stream); TestRFC2865ResponseAuthenticatorCoversEveryNamedField mutates each named field and asserts VerifyResponseAuth rejects it.

RFC2865-3-7.note: Forbidden: accepting a packet shorter than its Length field. TestDecodeRefusesAPacketShorterThanItsLengthField sets Length to len+1 and requires Decode to error; the positive decodes an exact-length packet.

RFC2865-4.1-2.note: Forbidden: an Access-Request with neither NAS-IP-Address nor NAS-Identifier. radius TestAdminAccessRequestIdentifiesTheNAS asserts hasIP || hasID on the wire; authradius TestRFC2865AccessRequestNamesTheNASWithNoIdentityConfigured asserts a non-empty NAS-Identifier even with nothing configured (red if the request goes out naming no NAS).

RFC2865-4.1-3.note: Judge 2026-09-30 (cont 5/6). Both points of the 2026-09-29 weak verdict are closed. (1) The row now quotes the whole Section 4.1 span through 'If future extensions allow other kinds of authentication information to be conveyed, the attribute for that can be used in an Access-Request instead of User-Password or CHAP-Password.', verbatim, so the MS-CHAPv2 unit (MS-CHAP2-Response, no User-Password/CHAP-Password) proves a request the row permits. The middle 'MUST NOT contain both' sentence rides in the span; TestAdminAccessRequestCarriesExactlyOneCredential (tagged here and 4.1-4) and the MS-CHAPv2 and EAP units each assert neither RFC 2865 credential beside the one sent. (2) TestRFC2865EAPAccessRequestCarriesTheExtensionCredential drives a full EAP-MSCHAPv2 admin login against the mock server and asserts, per captured Access-Request, EAP-Message present, no User-Password, no CHAP-Password, and exactly one State on every request after the first; recorded red on eapCredential. Positives: PAP User-Password, CHAP CHAP-Password, admin one-credential, MS-CHAPv2 and EAP extension credentials. Negatives: AuthMethodNone and a short MS-CHAPv2 response each put no Access-Request on the wire (no credential, no request), which is the refusal this MUST can have.

RFC2865-4.2-1.note: Judged 2026-09-30 (rfc/full/rfc2865.txt:1015-1018, Section 4.2, 'Invalid packets are silently discarded.', MUST under D-3). Forbidden: a client trusting an Access-Accept whose Response Authenticator does not verify. TestClientAuthenticatorVerify answers the first attempt with an Accept signed with the wrong secret and every later one correctly signed: attempts >= 2 fails if the first reply is accepted rather than dropped (the client retransmits only when it discarded it), and the Code assertion fails if the correctly signed reply is not accepted. Only the secret differs between the two replies, so the buffer isolates the authenticator. Producer packet.go::VerifyResponseAuth via Client.Exchange; both polarities recorded and observed red. Tags moved from the retired RFC2865-3-4 under ruling R11; test body unchanged.

RFC2865-4.4-1.note: The L2TP half is now proven at authradius handler.go doRADIUS: an Access-Challenge (State + Reply-Message) to PAP and CHAP-MD5 subscriber logins is refused with exactly one answer to PPP, and the same logins with an Access-Accept (Framed-User) are admitted, so the refusal is specific to the Challenge code. The admin PAP half was already enforced (ErrAuthRejected, chain stops).

RFC2865-5-1.note: Forbidden: an Access-Request without User-Name when the name is available. The admin (radius TestRFC2865AccessRequestUserName) and L2TP (authradius buildAuthAttrs test) units assert User-Name present with the right value; the negative TestRFC2865AccessRequestOmitsAnUnavailableUserName covers the if-available condition.

RFC2865-5-2.note: Positive reads the Length octets EncodeTo writes on the wire (3, 8, 255 for 1/6/253-octet values, walking exactly to the packet end) and Decode reads Length 8 as "netops". Negative: a Filter-Id "netops" with Length octet 6 (value-only count) is refused; a decoder counting only the Value would accept it and go red. The old round-trip units stay floor assertions.

RFC2865-5-6.note: Negative drives Access-Accept, Access-Reject and Access-Challenge each with Length 1 and with a Length 5 past the packet end, re-signed so the Response Authenticator verifies (asserted) and only the length is wrong; Client.Exchange returns an error with no packet (silent discard). Positive delivers Reject and Challenge with valid lengths and their Reply-Message. All three codes and both invalid-length shapes covered.

RFC2865-5-7.note: Forbidden: failing on an embedded null. TestAttributeValueWithAnEmbeddedNullRoundTrips asserts the value with a null round-trips whole (red on truncation); TestAnEmbeddedNullDoesNotEndTheAttributeWalk asserts the following attribute is still decoded.

RFC2865-5-8.note: Forbidden: sending text of length zero. TestZeroLengthAttributeIsOmitted asserts an empty Filter-Id is dropped from the encoded packet (Len 1), and the admin and L2TP units assert an empty User-Name produces no attribute; TestOneOctetAttributeIsNotOmitted is the negative that bounds the guard.

RFC2865-5-9.note: Judged 2026-09-30 (rfc/full/rfc2865.txt:1383-1385, Section 5, string data type). Forbidden: a string-typed attribute of zero octets on the wire. TestRFC2865ZeroLengthStringIsOmitted encodes State, Class, Proxy-State and CHAP-Challenge with empty values beside a User-Name through Packet.EncodeTo, decodes the wire and fails if the attribute is present or the attribute count is not 1. TestRFC2865OneOctetStringIsSent is the boundary control: the one-octet string 00 must reach the wire byte-equal, so an encoder that dropped every string, or every 0x00-valued one, goes red; it is labelled negative but is a conforming input, which is the only other polarity an emit-side MUST NOT has. Producer packet.go::EncodeTo omits any zero-length value at the wire boundary. Records observed red on both units.

RFC2865-5.11-1.note: Quote is the Filter-Id sentence of 5.11. Forbidden: Filter-Id content changing protocol operation. TestCarrierAttributesDoNotAffectAnAccessReject asserts a Reject carrying Filter-Id stays a rejection; TestCarrierAttributesDoNotAffectAnAccessAccept asserts an Accept carrying it stays an accept. Question reported: ze uses Filter-Id as its admin profile carrier.

RFC2865-5.2-1.note: Forbidden: a User-Password cipher not chained as MD5(S+RA) then MD5(S+c(i-1)). TestEncodeUserPasswordMultiBlock compares a 2-block ciphertext with one the test builds from the RFC recipe (red if block 2 is keyed on RA), TestEncodeUserPassword reverses block 1 with MD5(S+RA); the negatives assert the ciphertext changes with the secret and with the Request Authenticator.

RFC2865-5.2-2.note: Forbidden: a password not null-padded to a multiple of 16, or longer than 128. TestEncodeUserPassword asserts len%16 == 0 and the decoded pad octets are 0; TestEncodeUserPasswordEmpty asserts 16; TestEncodeUserPasswordMultiBlock asserts 32 and the chain over the null-padded plaintext; TestRFC2865UserPasswordClamp asserts 128 for a 130-octet input. Single-polarity marker on the row.

RFC2865-5.24-1.note: Forbidden: returning State modified or not at all. TestRadiusAdminStateIsReturnedUnmodified asserts each round's request carries that round's distinct State byte for byte (red on drop, rewrite or stale echo); TestRadiusAdminStateIsNotManufactured asserts no State when the challenge sent none.

RFC2865-5.25-1.note: Quote is the Class sentence of 5.25. Forbidden: interpreting Class locally. TestRadiusClassIsNotInterpretedLocally asserts an Accept whose only carrier is Class yields no profile and ErrAuthRejected; TestExtractRadiusConfigProfileAttrNeverClass asserts no configuration selects Class. Two tagged units (TestStateIsNotInterpretedLocally, TestRadiusAdminEapChallengeLoopCarriesState) prove the State rule of 5.24 instead, reported.

RFC2865-5.6-1.note: Judged 2026-09-30 (rfc/full/rfc2865.txt:1693-1696, Section 5.6). Forbidden: honouring an Access-Accept whose Service-Type the NAS does not implement or does not know. On the L2TP LNS, TestRFC2865UnknownOrUnsupportedServiceTypeIsARejection drives both halves of 'unknown or unsupported': Login-User 1 and Callback-Framed-User 4 (defined, not implemented) and 65535 (undefined), each alone in the Accept, and fails if the session comes up; the producer is doRADIUS calling radius.AcceptedServiceType(resp, ServiceTypeFramed) and answering respond(false). TestRFC2865SupportedServiceTypeIsHonored is the conforming input (Framed-User) and fails if a supported Service-Type is refused, ruling out a check that rejects every Accept. Buffers isolated: only Service-Type varies. Records: positive against AcceptedServiceType, negative against doRADIUS, both observed red (panic breaks, which prove reachability; the discriminating assertion is the per-value accept flag).
